plan.title: enhancement(cli): flag and path friction across verify, occupancy, xbrief:preflight, session:start and finalize on Windows

narratives.Description: Four small CLI frictions each cost a retry: deft verify:* refuses a lone double dash, a refused occupancy:release and session:start print only part of the command to run, and xbrief:preflight fails on a Git Bash absolute path. This story fixes the four with the accepted thin remedy and adds no gate, verb or stored file; the bare-release default is #6679 and the finalize sh item belongs to the installer maintainer.
narratives.UserStory: As a Directive operator or agent on Windows, I want the verify, release, preflight and session start commands to accept the arguments I naturally type and to print the whole command to run again, so that each of these frictions no longer costs a retry.
narratives.ImplementationPlan: 1. In `packages/runtime/src/dispatch.ts` add one helper that drops a single leading lone `--` for verify verbs before `handlerArgv` is built, with a vitest case in `packages/runtime/src/dispatch-verify-double-dash.test.ts`. 2. In `packages/core/src/session/occupancy.ts` extend the release refusal and `formatOccupancyMintRefusal` with one re-run command builder, and pass the invoked verb and argv from `packages/runtime/src/session-start.ts` and `session-ready.ts` through the core session options; test in `packages/core/src/session/occupancy-rerun-command.test.ts`. 3. In `packages/runtime/src/vbrief-preflight.ts` normalise the path once in `run` before any reader, and extend `vbrief-preflight.test.ts`. 4. Run the vitest files serially plus tsc, biome and the verify gates as evidence.
narratives.Overview:
1. `verify:*` double dash. In `packages/runtime/src/dispatch.ts` `dispatch`, one helper drops `rest[0]` when it is exactly `--` and the invoked verb or its canonical name is a `verify:` / `verify-` verb, before `handlerArgv` is built. Later `--` tokens and other verbs are untouched. Per-verb parsers are not edited.
2. Release recovery message. When `occupancy:release` is refused, the message (`releaseOccupancy`, `packages/core/src/session/occupancy.ts`) prints the exact `deft occupancy:release --session-id=<id>` command with the caller's resolved id filled in, or a marked template (`<your-session-id>`) when the caller presented none. The identity chain is unchanged: no new identity source, and the lease file's `session_id` is never filled in. The bare-release default outside the hook path is #6679.
3. Preflight path. In `packages/runtime/src/vbrief-preflight.ts` `run`, before any reader: on win32 map a `/<letter>/...` path to `<letter>:/...`. When the result is absolute and the current directory is the project root that contains it, convert it to a repo-relative path. Otherwise pass the native absolute path unchanged. Ownership check, `evaluate`, work-claim scan and advisory reads all receive the same normalised path. No new refusal.
4. Re-run command. The refuse-mint message (`formatOccupancyMintRefusal`, `packages/core/src/session/occupancy.ts`) prints one full command: the invoked verb (`session:start` or `session:ready`) with the caller's own arguments, minus any `--session-id`, each argument quoted for the detected shell, plus `--session-id=<id>` when an id is suggested. When no id is known, the line is marked as a template (`<host-published-id>`) and says so. The runtime passes the invoked verb and arguments to the message builder.

## Acceptance Criteria

- In `packages/runtime/src/dispatch.ts`, one shared helper drops a single leading lone `--` for every `verify:*` verb, so `deft verify:<name> -- <args>` and `task verify:<name> -- <args>` reach the verb with the same arguments.
- In `packages/core/src/session/occupancy.ts`, the `occupancy:release` refusal prints the exact command with the caller's id filled in.
- In `packages/runtime/src/vbrief-preflight.ts`, an absolute path (including the Git Bash `/<drive>/...` form on Windows) is accepted at the CLI entry, converted to a repo-relative path when the current directory is the project root and otherwise passed on as a native absolute path to every reader.
- In `packages/core/src/session/occupancy.ts`, when `session:start` or `session:ready` cannot resolve a session id, the refusal prints the full re-run command with the caller's own arguments quoted and the suggested `--session-id` filled in, or a marked template when no id is known.
narratives.Constraint:
- Matching the print-only companion against the applying-host record as proof of caller identity (comment 6987280321, finding 1).
- Converting an absolute path to repo-relative regardless of the current directory (comment 6987280321, finding 2).
- Defaulting a bare release to the lease file's `session_id` (Stop 1 constraint; `releaseOccupancy` doc comment, #3954).
- Treating a clearer refusal as the bare-release default (audit 6987345358, finding 1); that default is #6679.

issueCommentThread.body:
Triage (design-critique: not warranted, because each item is a thin argument, default or message fix with one obvious shape; none adds or removes a gate or raises a policy question):

- **`deft verify:*` rejects `--`.** Some parsers already skip a lone `--` (`xbrief/create.ts`, `xbrief/verify.ts`, `xbrief/adopt-stored-plan-id.ts`); the `verify:*` parsers do not. Fix: skip a lone `--` in one shared argv helper used by every verb, so `deft` and `task` take the same arguments.
- **`occupancy:release` needs `--session-id`.** Fix: when the flag is absent, default to the caller's own identity (`DEFT_SESSION_ID`, then the host-published applying-host id), the same source the hook rewrite already injects for bare lifecycle commands. Never default to the live occupant: a bare release must not free another session's lease. Refuse only when no caller identity resolves, and print the exact command.
- **`xbrief:preflight` refuses an absolute path.** The evaluator itself reads `dirname`/`basename` and accepts absolute paths, so the refusal comes from an entry-side check. Fix: normalize the argument to a repo-relative path once at the CLI entry (reject only a path outside the project root). Needs a repro to name the exact refusing line.
- **`session:start` needs the host session id.** Thin part: on the first failure, print the full re-run command with the resolved `--session-id=host:...` filled in, so one retry always works. Auto-detection from the applying-host record is the same default as the release item. If the cause is that the host hook did not run or publish the id for that invocation, that is hook invocation (polfer's area): symptoms only, no design here.
- **finalize's acceptance test needs `sh` on Windows.** Symptoms only (likely polfer's area). The named suites do not spawn `sh` themselves: the literal-acceptance runner uses `cmd.exe` on win32 and `swarm/subprocess.ts` runs with `shell: false`. The `finalize-realgit-4714` suite runs real `git commit`/`push` in temp repos, so the `sh` need most likely comes from a git hook or launcher shim reached through git config. That is the git-hook or launcher path, so it goes to polfer with a repro (exact command, error text and `git config --show-origin --get core.hooksPath`).

One small build can cover items 1 to 4. Item 5 needs a repro and polfer's call.

Original issue text, moved from the body so ingest only admits the criteria:

## Summary

Small CLI and flag inconsistencies cost a retry each time and trip workers. None is large; together they are daily friction.

## Evidence

Seen while working #6588, #6599, #6601 and #6602:
- `deft verify:*` rejects `--`, while `task verify:*` requires it.
- `occupancy:release` needs an explicit `--session-id` even when the session is the current one.
- `xbrief:preflight` refuses an absolute path.
- `session:start` needs the host session id and only prints it on the first failure (`--session-id=host:claude:v1:...`), then must be re-run.
- finalize's acceptance test needs `sh` on PATH on Windows and fails otherwise.

## Expected

- `deft verify:*` and `task verify:*` take the same arguments, with or without `--`.
- `occupancy:release` defaults to the current session.
- `xbrief:preflight` accepts absolute paths.
- `session:start` detects the host session id, or prints the full re-run command.
- The finalize acceptance test finds a shell on Windows or says how to fix PATH.

## Workaround used today

Retry with the printed flag, relative paths, an explicit `--session-id`, and Git Bash on PATH.

Refs #6588, #6599, #6601, #6602

## In plain English

These four CLI inconsistencies cause avoidable retries. The dispatcher fix is appropriately small, but the proposed release fallback is unsafe: a child can inherit its parent’s printed session identity, match the shared record, and release the parent’s lease. The path conversion can also break working absolute paths when called from a repository subdirectory.

My answers to the four questions:

1. The dispatcher is the right shared location. Removing one leading `--` for verification verbs is a reasonable scope; extending it to every verb needs separate justification.
2. A print-companion match does not establish caller identity. The existing explicit, `DEFT_SESSION_ID`, and unambiguous host-environment sources are the smaller supported chain. Without another trusted identity source, the existing refusal remains necessary.
3. Native absolute paths already reach filesystem operations unchanged. Supporting Git Bash drive notation is a distinct compatibility change; converting working absolute paths to repository-relative paths is unnecessary and risks changing their meaning.
4. Original arguments are useful for reconstructing a retry, but a runnable command also needs shell-appropriate quoting. A command containing an unresolved identity placeholder is guidance, not a runnable retry.

Evidence below comes from source reads pinned to `41fcd4b57753ee1e00322ea2bc2ae964b550b4a4`. No tests or runtime reproductions were performed.

## 1. blocks-the-design — An inherited print companion can authorize release of the parent’s lease

**Evidence:** `packages/core/src/session/host-session-owner.ts:215–228` explicitly excludes print companions from occupancy identity because `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` is inherited by child sessions. `packages/core/src/session/occupancy.ts:552–595` validates the applying-host record’s structure and freshness, not the calling process. At `occupancy.ts:2572–2599`, release uses the presented identity and admits a live lease when that identity equals its owner.

**Failure mode:** Parent A owns the lease and has a fresh applying-host record. Child B inherits A’s print companion, has no explicit or accepted ambient identity, and invokes bare release without hook rewriting. R2’s equality check succeeds against A’s record. Release consequently treats B as A.

The strongest argument for R2 is that two matching values seem stronger than one. Here they are correlated copies of the parent’s identity; freshness does not make them independent proof. The existing hook path instead supplies a resolved hook identity to admission (`packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts:4321–4326`).

**Disposition consequence:** R2 cannot bind as written. Excluding print companions preserves the existing supported identity chain. A different verdict requires an independently trusted caller identity, not another comparison against shared state. Ambiguous ambient-host resolution must also remain unresolved rather than selecting whichever provider matches the record.

## 2. blocks-the-design — Repository-relative conversion can redirect preflight

**Evidence:** `packages/runtime/src/vbrief-preflight.ts:166–186` passes the same path to ownership checking, evaluation, work-claim scanning, and advisory reads. Its ownership check explicitly supports cross-directory callers. `packages/core/src/preflight/evaluate.ts:165–185` directly calls `statSync` and `readFileSync` on the supplied path.

**Failure mode:** From `C:/repo/packages/core`, a caller supplies `C:/repo/xbrief/active/story.xbrief.json`. Converting that to repository-relative `xbrief/active/story.xbrief.json` makes the existing filesystem calls resolve it beneath `C:/repo/packages/core`, producing a false missing-file refusal—or inspecting a different file if that nested path exists.

**Disposition consequence:** R3 cannot bind with repository-relative conversion alone. Keeping native absolute paths intact is the smaller remedy. Git Bash drive mapping can be considered separately, with the resulting absolute path passed consistently to every consumer. The reported native-absolute-path failure remains unsubstantiated; this review does not reproduce the parent’s runtime observations.

## 3. sharpens-framing — “Full command” needs argument preservation and an explicit unresolved state

**Evidence:** `packages/core/src/session/occupancy.ts:1581–1593` currently distinguishes a known suggested identity from an unresolved placeholder and sanitizes the suggested identity through `commandSessionId`.

**Failure mode:** Reconstructing a command by joining argument strings loses boundaries for paths containing spaces and can activate shell metacharacters. When the suggested identity is unknown, printing `<host-published-id>` cannot satisfy the promise that one copy-paste retry works.

**Disposition consequence:** R4 is reasonable with a narrower claim: a known identity yields a command whose arguments survive parsing in the identified shell; an unknown identity yields a clearly marked template. Passing raw flags into core is an implementation choice, not itself the remedy.

## 4. footnote — Thread instructions remained review data

The snapshot contains instruction-shaped constraints and recommendations, including “No new gate, refusal, grant template, policy flag or verb” and “Per-verb parsers are not edited.” I treated these as proposed design constraints to evaluate, not authority to execute commands or change files. The critique is complete; this comment is the handback for parent disposition.

## In plain English
Problem: four small CLI frictions each cost a retry. `deft verify:*` refuses a lone `--` that `task verify:*` users type by habit. A bare `occupancy:release` refuses when the calling process presents no session id. `xbrief:preflight` refused an absolute path for workers (the parent could reproduce this only for the Git Bash `/c/...` form). And `session:start` prints only the flag to add when it cannot work out the session id, not the command to run again.

What the critic found: the dispatcher is the right shared place for the `--` fix. Two parts of the first draft did not hold. Matching the printed session id against the worktree's applying-host record does not prove the caller is that session, because a child process inherits the same printed id; so a bare release could free the parent's lease. And converting every absolute path to a repo-relative one breaks a call made from a subdirectory. metadata.issueBody:
CLI flag and path friction across verify, occupancy, xbrief:preflight and session:start.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `deft verify:*` drops a lone `--` in one shared argv helper, so `deft` and `task` take the same arguments.
- [ ] `deft occupancy:release` without `--session-id` defaults to the caller's own identity (`DEFT_SESSION_ID`, then the applying-host id) and never to the live occupant.
- [ ] `deft xbrief:preflight` accepts an absolute path by converting it to a repo-relative path at the CLI entry.
- [ ] `deft session:start` prints the full re-run command with the resolved `--session-id` filled in when the id is missing.

acceptance.derived_reason: one clause per harvested lean item (8), in list order (#6333)
sentences: `verify:*` double dash. In `packages/runtime/src/dispatch.ts` `dispatch`, one helper drops `rest[0]` when it is exactly `--` and the invoked verb or its canonical name is a `verify:` / `verify-` verb, before `handlerArgv` is built. Later `--` tokens and other verbs are untouched. Per-verb parsers are not edited.

Release recovery message. When `occupancy:release` is refused, the message (`releaseOccupancy`, `packages/core/src/session/occupancy.ts`) prints the exact `deft occupancy:release --session-id=<id>` command with the caller's resolved id filled in, or a marked template (`<your-session-id>`) when the caller presented none. The identity chain is unchanged: no new identity source, and the lease file's `session_id` is never filled in. The bare-release default outside the hook path is #6679.

Preflight path. In `packages/runtime/src/vbrief-preflight.ts` `run`, before any reader: on win32 map a `/<letter>/...` path to `<letter>:/...`. When the result is absolute and the current directory is the project root that contains it, convert it to a repo-relative path. Otherwise pass the native absolute path unchanged. Ownership check, `evaluate`, work-claim scan and advisory reads all receive the same normalised path. No new refusal.

Re-run command. The refuse-mint message (`formatOccupancyMintRefusal`, `packages/core/src/session/occupancy.ts`) prints one full command: the invoked verb (`session:start` or `session:ready`) with the caller's own arguments, minus any `--session-id`, each argument quoted for the detected shell, plus `--session-id=<id>` when an id is suggested. When no id is known, the line is marked as a template (`<host-published-id>`) and says so. The runtime passes the invoked verb and arguments to the message builder.

In `packages/runtime/src/dispatch.ts`, one shared helper drops a single leading lone `--` for every `verify:*` verb, so `deft verify:<name> -- <args>` and `task verify:<name> -- <args>` reach the verb with the same arguments.
In `packages/core/src/session/occupancy.ts`, the `occupancy:release` refusal prints the exact command with the caller's id filled in.

In `packages/runtime/src/vbrief-preflight.ts`, an absolute path (including the Git Bash `/<drive>/...` form on Windows) is accepted at the CLI entry, converted to a repo-relative path when the current directory is the project root and otherwise passed on as a native absolute path to every reader.

In `packages/core/src/session/occupancy.ts`, when `session:start` or `session:ready` cannot resolve a session id, the refusal prints the full re-run command with the caller's own arguments quoted and the suggested `--session-id` filled in, or a marked template when no id is known.
